test.name: Resolution rationale explains historically why the losing-side evidence exists
test.description: Birthplace conflict c_001 — Ireland (1850 and 1860 censuses) vs. Pennsylvania (1908 death certificate). The user explicitly asks why the contradiction exists, not just which source wins. Tests whether Part 4 of the resolution rationale uses historically grounded reasoning: delayed birth certificates compiled from secondary-informant recollection, Irish immigrants whose descendants assumed American birth decades later, and a son-in-law informant with no firsthand knowledge of a birth 63 years earlier.

input.delegation:
Resolve conflict c_001 — the birthplace discrepancy between the census records and the death certificate. I want to understand the historical reason why the death certificate says Pennsylvania when both census records say Ireland.

conflictId: c_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Never dock Part 4 of the persisted resolution_rationale (why the less reliable evidence exists) under Completeness or Correctness — it is graded ONLY under Evidence weighing. If the conflict is left open or deferred, Part 4 is not graded. Otherwise grade (a)-(c) across the whole resolution_rationale, not Part 4 alone; a fact stated in Part 3 counts. PASS: the rationale names or plainly describes the historical pattern behind the Pennsylvania entry (e.g. 'immigration-origin confusion', or 'would naturally give the state where the family had lived for decades') AND states (a) the informant's relationship to the subject, son-in-law (his name is not required), (b) that he could not have known the birthplace firsthand, stated or plainly evident from the text (e.g. 'knew the decedent only as a Pennsylvania resident'), and (c) the time elapsed as a figure (e.g. '63 years', 'about 60 years'). Naming or describing the pattern covers what he was likely reporting instead; the exact phrase 'locally familiar answer' is not required. PARTIAL: the pattern is named or described but one of (a)-(c) is missing. FAIL: no pattern is named or described, or the rationale cites 'Appendix B' or any instruction document. Do not synthesize extra grading dimensions beyond the rubric's

The independence of the two census sources (a_002 and a_009) and the shared-informant caveat (both may reflect the same household member's knowledge) should appear in the independence_analysis — the historical reasoning belongs in Part 4, not as a substitute for the independence assessment
